newsitem.title: UK: UK Conservatives attack govt over pension plans.
newsitem.headline: UK Conservatives attack govt over pension plans.

text.p: The main opposition Conservative party said on Wednesday the government would be guilty of mis-selling if it failed to inform Britons with personal pensions of the impact of its planned tax changes.

Peter Lilley, the Conservatives' main finance spokesman, said the government's plans to scrap dividend tax credits would cost pension funds five billion pounds a year, resulting in lower pensions unless employers and employees pay more in.

In particular, he said many people who had been advised to opt out of the state earnings-related pensions scheme (SERPS) to buy a personal pension should be told they would be better off opting back in.
"If Labour are serious about freedom of information, then this would be a good place to start," Lilley said.

The Treasury had published a "name and shame" list of firms that have been slow to compensate some 600,000 people who were mis-sold personal pensions, Lilley noted, adding: "It is clear the government is going to the top of that list if they don't give that information."
The Conservatives plan to raise the issue during Wednesday's continuing debate on the finance bill in the House of Commons.
Some five million people who have opted out of SERPS get a rebate, calculated by the government's actuary, to enable them to buy an equivalent personal pension.
But although scrapping the 20 percent dividend tax credit will reduce investment returns, the government says it has no plans for the next five years to alter the rebate, Lilley said.
"They are deliberately leaving people unprovided for," he said.

The government argues that many company pension schemes are in surplus and can easily absorb the tax change, but David Heathcoat-Amory, Lilley's deputy, said the effect would be dramatic, especially on the 75 percent of personal pensions that are money-purchase schemes.
